avisos.mensaje: Beneficio antes de impuestos: «IncomeLossFromContinuingOperationsBeforeIncomeTaxesDomestic» termina el 2025-12-31; solo se usa para años antiguos.
Beneficio antes de impuestos: «IncomeLossFromContinuingOperationsBeforeIncomeTaxesMinorityInterestAndIncomeLossFromEquityMethodInvestments» termina el 2021-06-30; solo se usa para años antiguos.
Gastos por intereses: «InterestExpense» termina el 2024-03-31; solo se usa para años antiguos.
Dividendos pagados: «PaymentsOfDividends» termina el 2026-03-31; solo se usa para años antiguos.
Amortizaciones (D&A): la compañía no usa la etiqueta combinada; se suman depreciación (us-gaap:Depreciation) y amortización de intangibles (us-gaap:AmortizationOfIntangibleAssets).
Acciones: se usan las diluidas medias del 3T26 (12,368 M).

eliminados: Through our products, we have an aspiration to help individuals, cities, and other partners collectively reduce one gigaton of their carbon equivalent emissions annually by 2030.

In 2021, we set an ambitious goal to reach net-zero emissions across all of our operations and value chain by 2030. To make progress toward this effort, we aim to reduce 50% of our combined Scope 1, Scope 2 (market-based), and Scope 3 absolute emissions (compared to our 2019 base year) by 2030, and we plan to invest in nature-based and technology-based carbon removal solutions to neutralize our remaining emissions.

Our primary approach to reducing our Scope 2 emissions is through the procurement of carbon-free energy (CFE). In 2020, we set a goal to run on 24/7 CFE every hour of every day on every grid where we operate by 2030. In 2023, we began implementing our carbon removals strategy, and we have begun establishing impactful partnerships and have started contracting for carbon removal credits.
We are a company of curious, talented, and passionate people. We embrace collaboration and creativity, and encourage the iteration of ideas to address complex challenges in technology and society.

As of December 31, 2024, Alphabet had 183,323 employees. noticias.titular: France Wants a 5.5-Cent-per-Gigabyte Tax on Netflix, Google and Meta
noticias.resumen: France just voted to bill Netflix, Google, and Meta by the gigabyte, and the revenue estimate runs into the billions. Whether it survives the Senate and a potential White House response is another matter entirely.
